channel.title: Self-Employed Taxes
channel.description: Quarterly estimated tax help for freelancers and side hustles.

item.title: 2026 Quarterly Estimated Tax Due Dates for Freelancers
item.description: The fourth 2026 estimated tax payment is due January 15, 2027. Self-employed people usually need to pay quarterly if they expect to owe $1,000 or more. The free calculator works out your payment with the IRS 1040-ES worksheet and safe harbor rules.

item.title: How Much to Set Aside for Taxes as a Freelancer (2026)
item.description: With no other income, a single freelancer with $60,000 of 2026 profit owes about $12,037 in federal income and self-employment tax, roughly 20%. Use the free calculator to get your own quarterly estimated tax payment, based on the IRS Form 1040-ES worksheet.

item.title: Estimated Tax Safe Harbor: Pay 100% of Last Year's Tax
item.description: You can avoid the underpayment penalty by paying the smaller of 90% of this year's tax or 100% of last year's (110% if your AGI was over $150,000). With $90,000 of profit and $9,000 of tax last year, that's $2,250 a quarter instead of $4,346. The free calculator follows the IRS Form 1040-ES worksheet.

item.title: Free Printable Mileage Log (PDF) for 2026 Taxes
item.description: A free one-page mileage log for business driving: date, destination, business purpose, odometer start and end, miles, and parking and tolls, the record items IRS Publication 463 lists. US Letter PDF, black and white, with a page explaining what to write and the 2026 rates (72.5 cents to June 30, 76 cents from July 1). No sign-up.

item.title: Self-Employment Tax Explained: 15.3% for Freelancers
item.description: Employees split Social Security and Medicare with their employer; self-employed people pay both halves: 15.3% on 92.35% of profit, with Social Security capped at $184,500 of earnings in 2026. Half of it is deductible. Work out yours with the free self-employment tax calculator.

item.title: Freelancer Tax Tracker Spreadsheet (Excel)
item.description: Log what you earn and spend; the spreadsheet sorts expenses into Schedule C lines, works out each quarterly estimated tax payment with the IRS worksheet, and tracks what you've paid against every due date. 2026 and 2027, all filing statuses.

item.title: Free Printable Daily Tip Log for Servers and Bartenders (PDF)
item.description: A free one-month tip log: cash tips, card tips, tips from others, tips paid out with names, and tips kept, the daily record IRS Publication 531 asks tipped employees to keep. Includes a box for the report due to your employer by the 10th of the next month and notes on the new tips deduction (up to $25,000 for 2025-2028). US Letter PDF, no sign-up.

item.title: Home Office Deduction Calculator: Simplified vs Regular
item.description: A freelancer renting a 1,000 sq ft apartment for $1,800 a month, with a 150 sq ft office, deducts $750 with the simplified method but $3,630 with the regular method (Form 8829). Compare both with your rent, utilities, and office size. Follows IRS Pub 587.

item.title: Free Printable Income and Expense Log for Self-Employed (PDF)
item.description: A free income and expense log for freelancers and small businesses: date, payer or payee, what it was for, a Schedule C line code, income, expense, and receipt kept. The 2026 Schedule C line key is printed on the sheet, and page 2 covers what IRS Publication 583 says your books must show. US Letter PDF, no sign-up.
